# bugs #3849: return of a struct value such as *p crashes the compiler or leaves the caller's object unwritten

- Ticket: https://sourceforge.net/p/sdcc/bugs/3849/
- Category: [Fixes](../../fix.md)
- Evidence: tested on r17193
- Recommended action: Apply after the patch for #3847. Check the ticket's example with -msm83, which was not tested, and close.
- Patch: [bugs-3849.patch](../../patches/bugs-3849.patch), commit [`90ef065a0`](https://github.com/mdmower/sdcc/commit/90ef065a05ab33766c035056bfe2d47c9449259a). Apply after `bugs-4157-1.patch`, `bugs-3121.patch`, `bugs-3847.patch`.
<!-- end of generated block -->

## Finding

The reporter gets SIGSEGV with `-msm83` for a function that returns `*((struct Test *)(&arg))`.
For mcs51 the compiler accepts the function without a diagnostic, and the code does not write the
caller's object. The mcs51 result is the same for every struct or union value that is not a
variable or a call: `*p`, `a[i]`, `s.m`, `p->m`, the value of a comma or assignment expression,
and a call that the compiler inlines. For z80 the test of this entry does not compile without the
patch. sm83 was not tested.

## Cause

The cause is the one of #3847. The front end gives the `RETURN` iCode a struct or union object as
its operand only when the expression is a variable. For the expressions above the operand is an
address, and the code generators have no code that returns a struct from an address.

## Fix

`geniCodeReturnStruct` in `src/SDCCicode.c`, which the patch for #3847 adds for calls, copies
every other such value to a temporary object and gives `RETURN` that object. It allocates one
temporary per function, in the way `geniCodeCall` allocates the result object of a call. The new
`createStructCopy` in `src/SDCCast.c` builds the copy with `rewriteStructAssignment`, so the copy
is the tree of a struct assignment. `createStructCopy` enters the temporary in the symbol table
while that tree is decorated, because the decoration of a call copies an argument that gets a
cast, and the copy looks up its symbols by name.

Each such `return` statement costs one `memcpy` call, and each function that has one costs storage
of the size of its return type. The code for `struct s r = *p; return r;` costs the same.

With this patch, `ast2iCode` does not pass a conditional expression to `geniCodeReturnStruct`,
because r17193 evaluates conditional expressions with struct operands wrongly by themselves
(#4131, #4163). mcs51 then reports error 172 for `return c ? a : b;` through the check that the
first patch of #4157 adds. The patch for #4131 corrects the evaluation and removes this exception,
and with it the statement compiles. This patch rewrites the comment at the check in
`src/mcs51/gen.c`, so it applies after the first patch of #4157.

## Verification

`support/regression/tests/bug-3849.c` has the ticket's function, the expressions listed above,
four `return` statements of different kinds in one function, a union, and a call whose argument
points to the object that receives the result. Without the patch 26 of the 27 assertions fail for
mcs51-small and mcs51-large-stack-auto, and the test does not compile for z80. With the patch it
passes on the host, for six mcs51 configurations (the four models, and small and large with
`--stack-auto`), for stm8, and for z80.

The suites were run with the patches for #3847 and #4157 also applied. valdiag has no failures for
mcs51, mcs51-large, mcs51-stack-auto, z80, and stm8. The regression suite has no failures for
mcs51-small, and no other test changes its code size.

## Related

- #3847 has the same cause for calls. This patch extends the function that its patch adds.
- #4157 is the same defect for mcs51.
- #4131 and #4163 are about conditional expressions with struct operands.
- #4250 reports the internal error of stm8 and z80 for `return w.in;`, which has the form `s.m`.
  On r17193 the function of that ticket returns wrong bytes for mcs51. With the whole series of
  this report applied, it returns the correct bytes in the six mcs51 configurations, and the file
  of the ticket compiles for stm8 and z80.
